key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, higher-velocity spray processes generally produced denser, harder coatings with better wear performance, while HVAF delivered the best overall corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: This study helps select thermal spray routes for extending service life of stainless-steel components exposed to abrasion and corrosive environments.
method: Applied WC-10Co-4Cr coatings to 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction/wear behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance.
Ranked coating performance across the four spray technologies to identify process-dependent tradeoffs.
evidence_signal: Compared with bare 304 stainless steel, coating hardness increased to 771.4–1166.2 HV, wear rate dropped from 36.82×10^-5 to as low as 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and HVAF showed the best corrosion metrics (−0.37 VSCE, 1.75 μA/cm², 20438.5 Ω).
watch_item: Performance rankings are specific to the tested spray parameters, so process optimization and adhesion/density control are critical before transferring these results to other substrates or service conditions.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
